mcqs.q: The trigeminal nerve is best described as the:
opts: Largest cranial nerve, mixed (large sensory + small motor)
A spinal nerve with autonomic fibres only
mcqs.explain: CN V is the largest cranial nerve and is mixed — a large sensory root and a small motor root.

mcqs.q: Which division of the trigeminal nerve carries motor fibres?
mcqs.explain: Only V3 (mandibular) is mixed; V1 and V2 are purely sensory, so V3 alone carries the motor fibres.

mcqs.q: The motor root unites with the sensory root of the mandibular division:
mcqs.explain: The separately-arising motor root joins the sensory root of V3 just below the foramen ovale to form a single trunk.

mcqs.q: Pain and temperature from the face relay mainly in the trigeminal:
mcqs.explain: The spinal nucleus relays pain and temperature; the mesencephalic nucleus handles proprioception/pressure and the principal nucleus discriminative touch.

mcqs.q: The trigeminal (Gasserian) ganglion lies in Meckel's cave at the apex of the:
opts: Petrous part of the temporal bone
mcqs.explain: The semilunar/Gasserian ganglion sits in a bony fossa (Meckel's cave) at the apex of the petrous temporal bone on the floor of the middle cranial fossa.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the ophthalmic nerve (V1) is correct?
opts: Supplies the lower lip and chin
mcqs.explain: V1 is the smallest division and is purely sensory, supplying the cornea, conjunctiva, upper lid, forehead, scalp and nose.

mcqs.q: The ophthalmic nerve enters the orbit through the:
mcqs.explain: V1 divides into lacrimal, frontal and nasociliary nerves which enter the orbit through the superior orbital fissure.

mcqs.q: The largest branch of the ophthalmic nerve, dividing into supratrochlear and supraorbital nerves, is the:
mcqs.explain: The frontal nerve is the largest V1 branch and divides into the supratrochlear and supraorbital nerves to the scalp; the lacrimal is the smallest.

mcqs.q: The maxillary nerve (V2) leaves the cranium through the:
mcqs.explain: V2 exits via the foramen rotundum (V3 uses the foramen ovale; the meningeal artery uses the foramen spinosum).

mcqs.q: The maxillary nerve is functionally:
mcqs.explain: Like V1, the maxillary division (V2) is purely sensory.

mcqs.q: After crossing the pterygopalatine fossa, the maxillary nerve continues as the:
mcqs.explain: V2 runs through the infra-orbital groove/canal and emerges at the infra-orbital foramen as the infra-orbital nerve.

mcqs.q: The nasopalatine nerve reaches the anterior palate (premaxilla) by passing through the:
mcqs.explain: The nasopalatine nerve crosses the nasal roof and descends through the incisive canal/foramen to supply the premaxilla.

mcqs.q: The greater palatine foramen typically opens in the palate:
opts: Distal to the maxillary second molar
In the midline of the soft palate
mcqs.explain: The greater palatine nerve emerges at the greater palatine foramen, distal to the second molar, to supply the posterior hard palate.

mcqs.q: Which superior alveolar nerve supplies the maxillary molars?
mcqs.explain: The PSA supplies the maxillary molars (often except the mesiobuccal root of the first molar), sinus and molar gingiva.

mcqs.q: The mesiobuccal root of the maxillary first molar is usually supplied by the:
mcqs.explain: The MSA supplies the premolars and the mesiobuccal root of the first molar; this overlap explains why a PSA block may miss that root.

mcqs.q: The anterior superior alveolar (ASA) nerve gives pulpal supply to the:
mcqs.explain: The ASA supplies the maxillary incisors and canine, their bone and labial mucoperiosteum.

mcqs.q: The mandibular nerve (V3) differs from V1 and V2 in that it is:
opts: The largest division and the only mixed one
The smallest division and purely sensory
mcqs.explain: V3 is the largest division and the only mixed one (sensory + motor).

mcqs.q: Both roots of the mandibular nerve exit the skull through the:
mcqs.explain: The sensory and motor roots of V3 leave through the foramen ovale and unite in the infratemporal fossa.

mcqs.q: The motor fibres of V3 supply the muscles of mastication plus:
opts: Tensor tympani, tensor palatini, mylohyoid and anterior belly of digastric
Orbicularis oculi and the tongue muscles
mcqs.explain: Besides the four muscles of mastication, V3 motor fibres supply tensor tympani, tensor palatini, mylohyoid and the anterior belly of digastric.

mcqs.q: The only sensory branch of the anterior division of V3 is the:
mcqs.explain: The buccal (long buccal) nerve is the only sensory branch of the anterior division; the masseteric and deep temporal nerves are motor.

mcqs.q: The inferior alveolar nerve enters the mandible through the:
mcqs.explain: The IAN enters the mandibular foramen and runs in the inferior alveolar canal below the teeth.

mcqs.q: The terminal branch of the inferior alveolar nerve that emerges to supply the lower lip and labial gingiva is the:
mcqs.explain: The mental nerve exits the mental foramen to supply the lower lip and labial gingiva; the incisive nerve continues within bone to the anterior teeth.

mcqs.q: The lingual nerve carries taste from the anterior tongue because it receives the:
mcqs.explain: The lingual nerve receives the chorda tympani from the facial nerve, adding taste fibres to its general sensory supply of the tongue.

mcqs.q: The lingual nerve is at greatest surgical risk because it lies approximately:
opts: 1 cm below and behind the mandibular third molar
Inside the mandibular canal with the IAN
mcqs.explain: The lingual nerve lies about 1 cm below and behind the third molar in the gingiva, vulnerable during lower wisdom-tooth surgery.

mcqs.q: The auriculotemporal nerve characteristically:
opts: Arises by two roots that encircle the middle meningeal artery
Carries taste to the posterior tongue
mcqs.explain: The auriculotemporal nerve arises by two roots encircling the middle meningeal artery and lies behind the TMJ near the parotid.

mcqs.q: On a panoramic (OPG) radiograph, the inferior alveolar canal is an important landmark because it:
opts: Marks the IAN, which can be injured during lower third-molar surgery
Indicates the position of the lingual nerve
mcqs.explain: The canal carries the IAN beneath the molar/premolar roots; its proximity to impacted lower third molars risks nerve injury during extraction.

mcqs.q: The mylohyoid nerve is unusual among IAN branches because it:
opts: Is motor and branches off before the nerve enters the mandibular foramen
mcqs.explain: The mylohyoid nerve leaves the IAN before it enters the mandibular foramen and is motor to the mylohyoid and anterior belly of digastric.

mcqs.q: Trigeminal neuralgia is most often caused by:
opts: Compression of the nerve root by the superior cerebellar artery
A pulpal abscess of a molar
mcqs.explain: Neuralgia is usually due to an enlarged superior cerebellar artery compressing the nerve root near the pons, injuring the myelin sheath.

mcqs.q: Which set correctly pairs each division with its bony exit?
opts: V1 superior orbital fissure · V2 foramen rotundum · V3 foramen ovale
V1 foramen ovale · V2 foramen rotundum · V3 superior orbital fissure
V1 foramen rotundum · V2 foramen ovale · V3 superior orbital fissure
V1 optic canal · V2 foramen spinosum · V3 foramen rotundum
mcqs.explain: V1 exits via the superior orbital fissure, V2 via the foramen rotundum, and V3 via the foramen ovale.

mcqs.q: The buccal nerve supplies the buccal gingiva as far forward as the:
opts: Mesial of the first mandibular molar
Distal of the third molar only
mcqs.explain: The (long) buccal nerve supplies cheek skin/mucosa and the buccal gingiva up to the mesial aspect of the first mandibular molar.

saqs.q: Name the three divisions of the trigeminal nerve and state which carry motor fibres.
saqs.a: Ophthalmic (V1) — sensory only; Maxillary (V2) — sensory only; Mandibular (V3) — mixed (sensory + motor). Only V3 carries motor fibres.

saqs.q: List the trigeminal sensory nuclei and the modality each relays.
saqs.a: Mesencephalic — proprioception/pressure; Principal (pontine) — discriminative touch; Spinal — pain and temperature.

saqs.q: Through which bony opening does each division leave the skull?
saqs.a: V1 → superior orbital fissure; V2 → foramen rotundum; V3 → foramen ovale.

saqs.q: Name the three branches of the ophthalmic nerve (V1).
State the teeth supplied by the PSA, MSA and ASA nerves.
saqs.a: PSA — maxillary molars (often except the MB root of the 1st molar); MSA — premolars + MB root of the 1st molar; ASA — incisors and canine.

saqs.q: List the branches of the inferior alveolar nerve.
saqs.a: Pulpal branches to molars/premolars, the incisive nerve (to anterior teeth), the mental nerve (lower lip/labial gingiva), and the mylohyoid nerve (motor, given off before the mandibular foramen).

saqs.q: Define trigeminal neuralgia and give its usual cause.
saqs.a: Episodes of intense, electric-shock-like facial pain lasting seconds, triggered from a sensitive zone (touch/air). Usually caused by compression of the nerve root by the superior cerebellar artery, damaging the myelin sheath.
